database_summary: This is an e-commerce/orders dataset (SQLite) with customers, sellers, orders, order items, payments, product catalog and geolocation data plus order reviews and a product-category translation table. Tables include both current-state descriptive tables (customers, sellers, products) and event/transaction tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews). Geolocation contains many rows per zip prefix (historical/measurement-like). Primary business grain centers on orders and order items. Joins between orders -> order_items -> products -> sellers -> customers are common but can multiply rows when joining one-to-many relationships.

accepted.name: orders_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- derived normalized timestamps as ISO strings (preserve original columns too)
  CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_approved_at = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_estimated_delivery_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date_normalized
FROM olist_orders
accepted.description: Canonicalized order-level relation: one row per order with parsed timestamps and key order status and customer reference. Use for joining to payments/items/reviews or for time-based analyses. | Use for: order lifecycle timelines; orders by status or purchase date; join-ready orders for aggregation with items/payments/reviews

accepted.name: order_items_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value
FROM olist_order_items
accepted.description: One row per order item with price and freight measures, preserving product and seller keys. Use as basis for item-level revenue, seller performance and product analyses. | Use for: item-level revenue and freight analysis; per-seller or per-product aggregates; shipping deadline vs delivery timing when joined with orders

accepted.name: payments_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  payment_sequential,
  payment_type,
  payment_installments,
  payment_value
FROM olist_order_payments
accepted.description: Payment attempts per order preserving sequential index, type, installments and value. Useful for payment-method analytics and joining to orders. | Use for: payment method distribution and amounts; analysis of multi-part payments (installments); join payments to orders for revenue reconciliation

accepted.name: products_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm
FROM olist_products
accepted.description: Product dimension at one row per product with descriptive and size/weight measures. Use for product-level aggregation and joins. | Use for: product sizing and weight distributions; category-level sales when joined to order items; product enrichment and translations

accepted.name: customers_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  customer_unique_id,
  customer_zip_code_prefix,
  customer_city,
  customer_state
FROM olist_customers
accepted.description: Customer dimension: one row per customer preserving both internal id and customer_unique_id and location attributes for geospatial/cohort analysis. | Use for: customer location distribution; repeat-customer analysis using customer_unique_id; join customers to orders for CRM metrics

accepted.name: sellers_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  seller_id,
  seller_zip_code_prefix,
  seller_city,
  seller_state
FROM olist_sellers
accepted.description: Seller dimension: one row per seller with location attributes for seller-level summaries and joins. | Use for: seller geographic distribution; seller performance when joined to order_items/orders

accepted.name: geolocation_zip_median
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  COUNT(*) AS sample_count
FROM olist_geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Aggregated geolocation per zip prefix: median latitude/longitude and a sample count. Use to map zip prefixes to a representative lat/lng. | Use for: map customers/sellers to lat/lng by zip prefix; visualization of geographic distribution of orders or customers

accepted.name: orders_with_items_payments
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  p.payment_sequential,
  p.payment_type,
  p.payment_installments,
  p.payment_value
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-item-payment relation: one row per order_item preserving order, item, product and payment attributes. Useful for revenue attribution and per-item payment analysis. Note: joining payments multiplies rows; payments are kept at their sequential level. | Use for: per-item revenue by payment method; analysis of orders with multiple payments or items; seller revenue by payment type

accepted.name: order_review_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(review_id) AS review_count,
  AVG(review_score) AS review_score_avg,
  MAX(review_creation_date) AS review_last_created_at
FROM olist_order_reviews
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: One row per order summarizing review metrics: average and count of review_score and latest review timestamp. Use for joining order sentiment to orders or customers. | Use for: order sentiment and review coverage; join review aggregates to orders/customers for NPS-like metrics

accepted.name: product_category_translation
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english
FROM olist_products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: Map product category codes to English names. One row per product_id with both original and english category when available. Useful for readable category-level reporting. | Use for: category-level sales with readable category names; translate product_category_name for dashboards and exports

accepted.name: customer_order_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(order_id) AS orders_count,
  MIN(order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_purchase_timestamp,
  MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_order_purchase_timestamp
FROM olist_orders
GROUP BY customer_id
accepted.description: Customer-level order counts and first/last purchase timestamps. One row per customer (customer_id). Useful for retention, recency and frequency analyses. | Use for: RFM/recency-frequency analyses; cohorting customers by first purchase

accepted.name: latest_review_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  review_id,
  order_id,
  review_score,
  review_comment_title,
  review_comment_message,
  review_creation_date,
  review_answer_timestamp,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY review_creation_date DESC) AS review_rank
FROM olist_order_reviews
accepted.description: Latest review per order using review_creation_date. One row per order for the most recent review. Use to attach the latest textual feedback to orders. | Use for: attach latest review to orders; filter to latest review per order by review_rank <= K downstream

accepted.name: seller_revenue_rolling
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.seller_id,
  o.order_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  (oi.price + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS item_total,
  SUM(oi.price + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY oi.seller_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS seller_revenue_cumulative
FROM olist_order_items oi
LEFT JOIN olist_orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
accepted.description: Seller-level running total revenue ordered by order purchase timestamp. One row per order_item per seller exposing cumulative revenue; useful for trend and cumulative-share analyses. | Use for: seller cumulative revenue over time; identify sellers reaching revenue milestones
